reasons: Both answers are strong and nearly equivalent: each opens with a user-framed problem, flags the thin evidence, has an explicit out-of-scope list, and gives As a/I want/so that stories with Given/When/Then edge cases. B's success metrics add a 'Measured by' column (ticket tags, analytics, event/audit logs, usability test), so each metric has a clear way to be measured, while A leaves both baselines and targets as TBD with no measurement method. B also has slightly sharper acceptance criteria (a concrete 20/17/3 skip example, a selection-limit message, due date before issue date) and practical advice, such as warning the VP about the scope cut and noting that page size may make the 500 limit moot.
